title: 7.4 Solving Polynomial Equations in Factored Form

icans: I can use the Zero-Product Property to solve equations.
I can factor out the greatest common monomial factor of a polynomial.
I can solve polynomial equations by factoring out the GCF.

vocab: a _____________ written as a product of factors, like (x − 4)(x + 1)
a root that comes from a factor that __________ more than once

head: Two numbers with a product of 12
Two numbers with a product of 0

blocks.p: Graph y = (x − 2)(x + 3) in Desmos. Where does it cross the x-axis? ________________________
How do those x-values relate to the factors?

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Solving a factored equation: To solve a factored equation, set _______________ factor equal to 0.
Repeated roots: A root that comes from a factor that appears more than once is a _______________ root.
Solving by factoring: To solve by factoring: get ______ on one side, _______________, then use the Zero-Product Property.
Careful: Don’t divide both sides by x: you lose the solution _______________.

blocks.stem: The arch of a bridge can be modeled by y = −0.2(x − 4)(x − 24), where x and y are measured in feet and the x-axis is the water. How wide is the arch at the water?
